references.text: Establishes the principle that no one shall be sentenced to death based on only one witness, but requires multiple witnesses for a capital sentence.
Requires two or three witnesses to carry out a death sentence and forbids execution based solely on the testimony of one witness.
Jesus cites this principle in connection with church discipline, where two or three witnesses must confirm a case.
Paul refers to the principle of two or three witnesses in connection with his upcoming visit to the church in Corinth.
Paul applies the rule of two or three witnesses to accusations against elders in the church.
Refers to the Mosaic Law, where anyone who rejected the law died without mercy on the word of two or three witnesses.
Jesus refers to the law of two witnesses to confirm the validity of his own testimony together with the Father's testimony.
